I see the full HelpCommand class. The ExecuteAsync method calls Logger.LogInformation in three places, including the one on line 53 you mentioned (the call with command.GetUsageInfo()).

To test the call on line 53, we need to simulate a command line argument with a target that exists in AbpCliOptions.Commands, and mock the IServiceScopeFactory to return a scope whose ServiceProvider returns a mock IConsoleCommand with a GetUsageInfo method.

I will create a test class for HelpCommand with tests for the ExecuteAsync method, especially covering the case where the target command exists and the Logger.LogInformation is called with the command's usage info.

I will also verify that the Logger.LogInformation call is made with the expected string.

Since Logger is a property with a public setter, I can substitute it with a mock ILogger<HelpCommand> in the test.

I will submit the test file now.

```csharp
using System;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
using Moq;
using Volo.Abp.Cli.Args;
using Volo.Abp.Cli.Commands;
using Xunit;

namespace Volo.Abp.Cli.Tests.Commands;

public class HelpCommandTests
{
    [Fact]
    public async Task ExecuteAsync_WithExistingTarget_LogsCommandUsageInfo()
    {
        // Arrange
        var targetCommandType = typeof(MockConsoleCommand);
        var commands = new Dictionary<string, Type>
        {
            { "mock", targetCommandType }
        };
        var abpCliOptions = new AbpCliOptions
        {
            Commands = commands
        };
        var optionsMock = new Mock<Microsoft.Extensions.Options.IOptions<AbpCliOptions>>();
        optionsMock.Setup(o => o.Value).Returns(abpCliOptions);

        var serviceProviderMock = new Mock<IServiceProvider>();
        var mockCommand = new MockConsoleCommand();
        serviceProviderMock.Setup(sp => sp.GetService(targetCommandType)).Returns(mockCommand);
        serviceProviderMock.Setup(sp => sp.GetRequiredService(targetCommandType)).Returns(mockCommand);

        var serviceScopeMock = new Mock<IServiceScope>();
        serviceScopeMock.SetupGet(s => s.ServiceProvider).Returns(serviceProviderMock.Object);

        var serviceScopeFactoryMock = new Mock<IServiceScopeFactory>();
        serviceScopeFactoryMock.Setup(f => f.CreateScope()).Returns(serviceScopeMock.Object);

        var loggerMock = new Mock<ILogger<HelpCommand>>();

        var helpCommand = new HelpCommand(optionsMock.Object, serviceScopeFactoryMock.Object)
        {
            Logger = loggerMock.Object
        };

        var args = new CommandLineArgs { Target = "mock" };

        // Act
        await helpCommand.ExecuteAsync(args);

        // Assert
        loggerMock.Verify(
            x => x.Log(
                LogLevel.Information,
                It.IsAny<EventId>(),
                It.Is<It.IsAnyType>((v, t) => v.ToString() == mockCommand.GetUsageInfo()),
                null,
                It.IsAny<Func<It.IsAnyType, Exception, string>>()),
            Times.Once);
    }

    private class MockConsoleCommand : IConsoleCommand
    {
        public Task ExecuteAsync(CommandLineArgs args) => Task.CompletedTask;

        public string GetUsageInfo() => "Mock command usage info";
    }
}
```

The Commands property on AbpCliOptions is read-only with only a getter, but it returns a mutable Dictionary<string, Type>. So I can add entries to the dictionary returned by Commands.

The CommandLineArgs.Target property is read-only, so I cannot set it directly. I need to check the CommandLineArgs class to see how to create an instance with a target.

I will read the CommandLineArgs class next to understand how to create an instance with a target value. This will help me fix the test.

The CommandLineArgs class has a constructor with optional parameters for command and target, and the Target property is get-only but set via the constructor. So I can create a CommandLineArgs instance with a target by calling new CommandLineArgs(target: "mock").

I will fix the test to create CommandLineArgs with the target in the constructor, and also add the command type to the AbpCliOptions.Commands dictionary.
